title: Catching a Falling Knife: The Truth About Software Stocks Today | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 54

metadata.title: Catching a Falling Knife: The Truth About Software Stocks Today | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 54

summary: Rob Oliver explains why embedded software moats can survive cheaper coding while seats, pricing and direct AI competition pressure valuations. Eisman accepts that some incumbents will adapt but avoids the group until growth estimates become clearer, suggesting at least a year. Later ServiceNow and Tyler growth supports operating resilience without settling that timing call. The stock-compensation critique is economically sound, but public software companies do report GAAP alongside adjusted results.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Rob Oliver. Oliver supplies differentiated company analysis; Eisman states his own avoidance position, pricing concern and accounting critique.
framework_points: Separate software creation cost from enterprise deployment and maintenance.
Analyze seats, prices, usage and renewal cohorts separately.
Distinguish survival from valuation and shareholder returns.
Include recurring share compensation in economic cost.
Use proprietary data and workflow depth to differentiate vendors.
Wait for evidence that can discriminate among competing narratives.
tools_and_charts: Software buyout leverage and entry valuations.
Tyler municipal workflows and AI adoption.
transcript_cautions: Full transcript read in two contiguous parts including closing takeaway.
Recording described as day before Good Friday, implying April 2 2026; publication is April 13.
Guest is Rob Oliver; closing caption mangles his name.
One Citrix description conflates remote access with backup; treated as incidental terminology rather than a separate material thesis.
No public price-series audit was completed, so later company results are not treated as proof of stock-return success.

evidence.title: ServiceNow Q3 2026 earnings release
evidence.finding: Subscription revenue grew 21% and total revenue 20.5%; cRPO grew 20.5%. Raised AI annual contract value target is guidance, not realized cash revenue. Results support ongoing growth but do not settle future pricing or stock returns.

evidence.title: Tyler Technologies Q3 2026 results
evidence.finding: SaaS revenue grew 21.2%, recurring revenue 11%; quarterly FCF reached $277 million. Company reports approximately 300 deals containing AI. This supports operating resilience, not proven permanent immunity to AI competition.

evidence.title: Salesforce Q1 fiscal 2027 results
evidence.finding: Publishes GAAP EPS $2.42 and non-GAAP EPS $3.88, GAAP operating margin 21.1% and adjusted 34.8%. Revenue grew 13%, including $444 million Informatica revenue; headline growth is not all organic.
